question_text: A 62-year-old man presents to the office because of painless rectal bleeding for the past 3 months. He describes intermittent streaks of bright red blood on the toilet paper after wiping and blood on but not mixed within the stool. Occasionally, he has noted a small volume of blood within the toilet bowl, and he associates this with straining. For the past 2 weeks, he has noticed an 'uncomfortable lump' in his anus when defecating, which goes away by itself immediately afterwards. He says he has no abdominal pain, weight loss, or fevers. He is a well-appearing man that is slightly obese. Digital rectal examination shows bright red blood on the examination glove following the procedure. Anoscopy shows enlarged blood vessels above the pectinate line. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
